lever: redfirst: v13 plus one sentence group at the end of step 2: 'Before the first edit, run the issue's example as a python3 heredoc that asserts the result the issue asks for and, for one ordinary input, the result the code gives today. The first assert must fail now (if it passes, the example misses the bug, so change it); rerun the same check after each edit until both asserts pass.' Adds 72 Gemma tokens (v13's prompt is 840). Pinned by tests/test_v13_fastapi_levers.py.
why: WRONG_SEMANTICS (write-up docs/forty_two/tasks/fastapi_14986.md): 'do not store root_path in servers' was implemented as deleting the per-request insertion in all 5 runs that edited, which breaks the pass-to-pass test that a request with a root_path still lists it; the escape half was right in 2 of them. On our line p4_b1024 made its first source edit at 119 s with no check before it, checked only with tests/test_local_docs.py and submitted at 187 s with about 110 s left (MEASURED, fastapi_census.txt section 1); that test file passes on the unedited code (MEASURED on the Mac: 5 passed at base, kpar venv, fastapi_census.txt section 5), so it could not catch anything. The rule's two asserts are exactly what was missing: a check written from the issue text alone (second request with another root_path does not carry the first, a script-closing string in a Swagger config is not emitted raw, and, as the ordinary input, one request with a root_path lists it as it does today) is red at base, red on all 5 edited box patches (the ordinary assert fails on every deletion; the escape assert also fails on p4_b1024's patch) and green on gold (MEASURED: docs/forty_two/evidence/fastapi_check_replay.txt). The repo's own regression tests for root_path cannot even be collected in the competition env (inline_snapshot missing, write-up), so a self-written check is the only one available. Expected: maybe (0 of 12 L4 runs; p4 and p4_v7c were one hunk short at 92-114 s).
baseline: Box (A6000, pace proxy, 5 min): p4 (v5h2), p4_v7, p4_v7c, p4_v7d, p4_b1024 (v12-b1024, v13's parent), p4_v0t2 all failed it (0/6). Kaggle L4: 0 of 12. p4_v13 (v13 alone, one sample): failed (B-074 and P2_LOG 16:23Z: 0 solved among the first 13 ids, which include this one; trace not yet on the Mac).
regression_risk: The rule adds or changes a step before the first edit. On p4_b1024, 15 of the 28 solved tasks made their first source edit without a failing check before it (MEASURED, fastapi_census.txt section 2); a python check costs 10-17 s of model time per call on the box (docs/forty_two/TIMING.md section 4). Most exposed: rich_3506 and rich_3521 (first source edit at 273 and 270 s, resolved at 304 s through the fallback diff) and fastapi_14458 (resolved at 305 s). Tasks without a runnable example may spend one or two calls on a check that cannot be red (INFERRED). Inherits v13's text-call risk (below).
also_applies_to: Any hidden task of the 'stop storing / caching / mutating X' kind, where deleting the feature passes a naive check and the ordinary-input assert is what catches it; and any task where the agent's only check is an existing test file that already passes. Outside the 42: fastapi_14458 was resolved on p4_b1024 at the cap after three green checks and no red one (the rule fires there).
text_call_risk: v13 carries a fenced heredoc block in step 3, suspected in the p4_v13 fastapi_14487 row that wrote every tool call as text (B-074). This bundle inherits that block unchanged; the added sentences have no code fence, no backticks and no tool-call syntax (tested). The leak predates v13: 5 of 1,783 replies on p4_b1024 (fastapi_14487 among them), 1 on p4_v0t2, 3 on p4, 1 on p4_v7, all recovered after the nudge (MEASURED: scripts/forty_two/text_call_leaks.py, fastapi_census.txt section 3). Read the queue run's traces for zero-call rows before reading its score.
